es.summary: Obstrucción crónica de arterias periféricas por aterosclerosis que reduce el flujo sanguíneo a extremidades, principalmente piernas. Se manifiesta con claudicación intermitente, cambios cutáneos y riesgo de ulceración o amputación.
key_points: Tabaquismo es el factor de riesgo más fuerte
Claudicación intermitente es el síntoma clásico
Manejo incluye control de factores de riesgo y revascularización

pathophysiology: Acumulación de placa de colesterol y grasa en la íntima arterial
Estrechamiento reduce el flujo sanguíneo distal
Isquemia crónica produce dolor muscular al ejercicio
En casos graves, se produce necrosis tisular y posible amputación
signs_symptoms: Claudicación intermitente: dolor, pesadez o calambres al caminar
Cambios de color: piel pálida o cianótica
Úlceras o heridas que cicatrizan lentamente
Temperatura del miembro afectado <2 °C respecto al contralateral
diagnostics: Doppler arterial o ecografía duplex para localizar estenosis
Angiografía por TC o MR para planificación quirúrgica
Perfil lipídico: colesterol total, LDL, HDL, triglicéridos
Glucosa en ayunas: >126 mg/dL sugiere diabetes
treatment: Control estricto de factores de riesgo (dejar de fumar, controlar glucosa y presión arterial)
Estatinas para reducir colesterol LDL <70 mg/dL
complications: Isquemia crítica que compromete la vida del tejido
nursing_care: Evaluar pulsos, temperatura y color de extremidades cada turno
Monitorear dolor con escala 0‑10 y registrar patrón de claudicación
Promover ejercicio supervisado y programa de caminata progresiva
Administrar y educar sobre aspirina y estatinas
Observar signos de infección o deterioro de la herida
patient_teaching: Dejar de fumar y buscar apoyo para cesación
Controlar glucosa y presión arterial según indicaciones médicas
Realizar caminatas diarias, aumentando gradualmente la distancia
Inspeccionar pies y piernas diariamente; reportar cambios de color o dolor
Mantener dieta baja en grasas saturadas y rica en fibra

evidenced_by: dolor en piernas al caminar menos de 100 m
fatiga y limitación de la marcha
outcomes: Capacidad de caminar: aumentar distancia a 150 m sin dolor en 2 semanas
Nivel de dolor: <3/10 en escala de dolor al final de la semana

interventions.action: Diseñar programa de caminata progresiva: 5 min, aumentar 1 min cada día
interventions.rationale: Mejora colateralización y tolerancia al ejercicio

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de reposo activo (detener y descansar 1‑2 min cada 5 min)
Monitorear y registrar nivel de dolor antes y después del ejercicio
interventions.rationale: Permite ajustar la intensidad del programa

interventions.action: Fomentar hidratación adecuada (≥2 L/día) y nutrición balanceada

en.summary: Chronic obstruction of peripheral arteries by atherosclerosis that reduces blood flow to extremities, primarily the legs. It presents with intermittent claudication, skin changes, and risk of ulceration or amputation.
key_points: Smoking is the strongest risk factor
Intermittent claudication is the classic symptom
Management includes risk factor control and revascularization

pathophysiology: Accumulation of cholesterol and fat plaque in the arterial intima
Chronic ischemia produces muscle pain with exercise
In severe cases, tissue necrosis and possible amputation occur
signs_symptoms: Intermittent claudication: pain, heaviness or cramps when walking
Color changes: pale or cyanotic skin
Ulcers or wounds that heal slowly
Temperature of affected limb <2 °C compared to contralateral
diagnostics: Arterial Doppler or duplex ultrasound to locate stenosis
CT or MR angiography for surgical planning
Lipid profile: total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides
treatment: Strict control of risk factors (quit smoking, control glucose and blood pressure)
Statins to reduce LDL cholesterol <70 mg/dL
nursing_care: Assess pulses, temperature, and color of extremities each shift
Monitor pain with 0‑10 scale and record claudication pattern
Promote supervised exercise and progressive walking program
Administer and educate about aspirin and statins
Observe for signs of infection or wound deterioration
patient_teaching: Quit smoking and seek cessation support
Control glucose and blood pressure as directed by healthcare provider
Inspect feet and legs daily; report color changes or pain

evidenced_by: pain in legs when walking less than 100 m
outcomes: Walking ability: increase distance to 150 m without pain in 2 weeks
Pain level: <3/10 on pain scale at end of week

interventions.action: Design progressive walking program: 5 min, increase 1 min each day
interventions.rationale: Improves collateral circulation and exercise tolerance

interventions.action: Teach active rest techniques (stop and rest 1‑2 min every 5 min)
Monitor and record pain level before and after exercise
Encourage adequate hydration (≥2 L/day) and balanced nutrition

summary.0.quote: Arterial insufficiency occurs when arterial blood flow is reduced due to atherosclerotic blockages.

summary.1.quote: If severe enough, blocked blood flow can cause tissue death and can sometimes lead to amputation of the foot or leg.

key_points.0.quote: The cause of PAD is atherosclerosis .

key_points.1.quote: The main risk factor for PAD is smoking.

key_points.2.quote: A primary symptom of peripheral vascular disease is intermittent claudication , a cramp-like muscle pain, burning sensation, or extreme fatigue in the calf, thigh, or buttocks that is induced by exercise and relieved by rest.

key_points.4.quote: More severe cases of arterial insufficiency may require surgical intervention such as angiography , endovascular repair, or arterial bypass ( Figure 12.36 ).

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Plaque is a substance made up of fat and cholesterol.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: It causes the arteries to narrow or become blocked.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: A primary symptom of peripheral vascular disease is intermittent claudication , a cramp-like muscle pain, burning sensation, or extreme fatigue in the calf, thigh, or buttocks that is induced by exercise and relieved by rest.

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: If severe enough, blocked blood flow can cause tissue death and can sometimes lead to amputation of the foot or leg.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: The main risk factor for PAD is smoking.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Other risk factors include older age and diseases like diabetes, high blood cholesterol, high blood pressure, heart disease, and stroke.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Medical therapies include pharmaceuticals, including statins and antiplatelet/anticoagulation agents, hypertension management if present, diabetes management if present, exercise, and smoking cessation as necessary.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: A primary symptom of peripheral vascular disease is intermittent claudication , a cramp-like muscle pain, burning sensation, or extreme fatigue in the calf, thigh, or buttocks that is induced by exercise and relieved by rest.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Weak or absent pulses in the legs or feet

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: A pale or bluish color to the skin

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Sores or wounds on the toes, feet, or legs that heal slowly, poorly, or not at all

sections.treatment.0.quote: The main risk factor for PAD is smoking.

sections.complications.0.quote: Chronic, or advanced, insufficiency can result in damage to the tissue of the extremities, including ulceration and gangrene.

sections.complications.1.quote: The patient’s wounds will reduce in size and be free of signs and symptoms of infection.

sections.complications.2.quote: If severe enough, blocked blood flow can cause tissue death and can sometimes lead to amputation of the foot or leg.

sections.complications.3.quote: Acute or critical limb ischemia may occur if left untreated.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: The patient’s wounds will reduce in size and be free of signs and symptoms of infection.
